title: Red canopies, toy soldiers and a clock tower
label: Brand gallery
lede: Four photographs and an engraving of the real stores, from freely licensed sources, and our own drawings in the same spirit.

archive.caption: “F.A.O. Schwarz, 42 East 14th Street, Union Square,” from King’s Handbook of New York City.
archive.alt: Engraving of the Schwarz Toy Bazar building
archive.credit: Scanned by the British Library, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:(King1893NYC)_pg866_F.A.O._SCHWARZ,_42_EAST_14TH_STREET,_UNION_SQUARE.jpg). Public domain.

archive.caption: The entrance at 767 Fifth Avenue, with a doorman in toy-soldier uniform, in March 2007, during the D. E. Shaw years.
archive.alt: Glass doors under a red canopy lettered F·A·O·Schwarz, with a doorman saluting
archive.credit: Photo: Rob Young, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:FAO_Schwarz_Front.jpg), CC BY 2.0.

archive.caption: The floor piano on the upper level of the Fifth Avenue store, March 2007.
archive.alt: Visitors standing on a giant piano keyboard
archive.credit: Photo: Rob Young, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Giant_Piano_in_FAO_Schwarz_(897354293).jpg), CC BY 2.0.

blocks.title: The front door, then and now
blocks.source: Photographs from Wikimedia Commons; credits and licenses above.

drawings.title: The door.
drawings.caption: A doorman dressed as a toy soldier stood at the Fifth Avenue entrance. Our drawing, not an official asset.

drawings.title: The piano.
drawings.caption: The floor piano from “Big,” which the new store brought back.[^29] Original illustration.

drawings.title: The clock.
drawings.caption: Each store had animated displays “highlighted by a signature FAO Schwarz clock tower.”[^1] Original illustration, not a copy of the real one.

drawings.title: The horse.
drawings.caption: A rocking horse was the company’s long-standing emblem, according to a reference history.[^9] This is our own drawing, not the trademarked mark.

disclaimer: Colors were matched by eye to the 2007 photograph of the Fifth Avenue entrance and are approximate. FAO Schwarz is a trademark of its owner and appears here in historical and editorial context. Drawings are original illustrations, not official assets.
